parts.title: A useful inbox, then a real answer
parts.intent: Help an operator investigate a synthetic incident without giving the AI permission to change a system.
parts.input: Select TRAIN-101, Payments slow after a release. Request: Analyze this synthetic incident using read-only evidence.
actions: Create a synthetic ticket; search and filter it.
Select TRAIN-101 and sign in to the app, separately from the builder workspace.
Choose Analyze safely once and inspect the returned answer.
parts.expected: An actual model answer separates observations, uncertainties and safe next checks. Payments p95 is 1,800 ms and errors are 1.2% in the synthetic fixture. Release r42 is a correlation, not a confirmed cause.
parts.appearance: A ticket inbox on the left; selected ticket, analysis request and readable answer on the right. Loading, sign-in and failure states are visible.
parts.status: Native Lovable app journey browser-verified; other builders require their own rehearsal.
parts.remaining: Learners must run their own app; static GitHub Pages never calls a model.

parts.title: Open the engine, keep the app
parts.intent: Make the harness visible: authorization, bounded model loop, validated tools, final answer and trace events.
parts.input: Repeat the selected synthetic incident, then test an unknown tool and an argument outside the selected service scope in isolated tests.
actions: Keep the same inbox and Analyze safely action.
Inspect the server tool registry and strict argument validation.
Open the actual run inspector after one successful investigation.
parts.expected: Only service_health and release_diff can execute in the Lovable example. The observed successful run used both tools and two model calls, below its three-call limit. Rejected tool cases must be checked in code tests.
parts.appearance: An expandable inspector below the answer shows actual model/tool events. A teaching animation explains these events but is not a live trace.
parts.status: Actual native model/tool events browser-verified; local harness contracts tested separately.
parts.remaining: A screenshot cannot prove all tool-validation or injection-resistance properties.

parts.title: Measure the answer, then compare models
parts.intent: Make latency, usage and estimated cost understandable without inventing a price or a winning model.
parts.input: Use the same synthetic task for each explicitly selected, available model. Keep tool inputs and limits fixed.
actions: Read provider-reported input and output usage from the real run.
Add matching sourced token rates only when available; otherwise show unknown.
If a second model is available, compare answer quality, tool behavior, latency and usage on the same task.
parts.expected: The reviewed Lovable run reported 761 input + 191 output = 952 total tokens and 5,218 ms. Estimated cost remained unknown. These are one run's observations, not a benchmark or a bill.
parts.appearance: A compact measurement panel beside the answer. Comparison rows distinguish reported tokens, illustrative arithmetic, estimated model cost and actual provider charges.
parts.status: Single-model usage browser-verified; cost arithmetic and missing-usage contracts locally tested.
parts.remaining: No live two-model comparison or provider billing readback is accepted for this Lovable rehearsal.

parts.title: Find the same action in Langfuse
parts.intent: See what the agent actually did, while excluding personal data, secrets and prompt content from workshop telemetry.
parts.input: Provide LANGFUSE_BASE_URL, LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY only through the app's server-side settings.
actions: Use the three-value instrumentation prompt with your current builder and existing LLM.
Run one synthetic investigation and retain its actual trace/session identifiers privately.
Find that exact trace in your own Langfuse project and check the root, authorization, actual generations and tools.
parts.expected: Expected structure: agent root → authorization; generation 1 → tools; generation 2 → answer. Export acknowledgment and independent readback are separate results. OCI APM spans and Log Analytics events require their own configured destinations and readback.
parts.appearance: Your real Langfuse project shows a trace tree and reported usage. Until configured, the app explicitly displays Langfuse not configured; no imitation dashboard is presented as evidence.
parts.status: Optional exporter code inspected; its eight isolated exporter tests passed locally, and missing-config UI was browser-verified. Live telemetry remains unverified.
parts.remaining: Needs a working learner-owned Langfuse project and exact readback. OCI APM/Log Analytics live readback is a separate acceptance gate.

parts.title: Ask for a change and watch it stop
parts.intent: Demonstrate that permission decisions belong in server code and every tool boundary, not only in a system prompt.
parts.input: Choose Test a change request in the authenticated app. Exercise malformed tools and controlled dependency failures in isolated tests.
actions: Trigger the explicit change-request control and inspect its response.
Verify zero model calls, then examine local tests for unknown tools, malformed arguments and safe failures.
parts.expected: approval_required; model not called; model calls 0 / 3. The actual app inspector reports an explicit server block. There is no automatic approval-resume or system-changing tool.
parts.appearance: A clear refusal beside the original ticket, with a zero-call inspector. Failures stay visible instead of being replaced with a fake answer.
parts.status: Explicit change-control path browser-verified; broader negative cases locally tested.
parts.remaining: This is not proof of universal prompt-injection prevention, production IAM enforcement or a complete application security audit.

parts.title: Prepare a hosted release you can verify
parts.intent: Move the working agent to an approved runtime with a defined identity, secrets, limits, health checks, rollback and observability.
parts.input: Use your own reviewed OCI scope and supported agent-hosting option; preserve the existing app and runtime compatibility.
actions: Review OCI AI Platform options and the Private Agent Factory walkthrough; confirm the selected runtime supports your app.
Prepare a deployment plan and exact resource/cost inventory before requesting deployment authority.
After an approved deployment, repeat create → select → analyze → change stop, then independently read back telemetry and test rollback.
parts.expected: A reviewed release packet with immutable artifact identity, permissions, secret references, health and canary results, exact telemetry readback and rollback procedure. A rendered plan alone never satisfies this gate.
parts.appearance: A deployment checklist showing source, artifact, runtime, canary, telemetry and rollback separately. Missing cloud access remains visibly pending.
parts.status: Local deployment/readiness contracts tested; this course's new hosted capstone is not live accepted.
parts.remaining: Requires current cloud access, named resources, deployment authority and a fresh signed-in canary/readback. Existing older deployments do not prove this app release.
